newsitem.title: USA: Oil inventories not positive long term - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Oil inventories not positive long term - Salomon.

text.p: Oil inventory trends are bullish for the market and oil-rich companies in the short term, but longer term patterns are less positive, according to Salomon Brothers analyst Paul Ting.

Pointing to industry and government reports showing a sharp drop in crude and oil product stocks last week, Ting said in a note to clients Wednesday: "This undoubtedly will have a bullish effect on prices in the short term...(and) should benefit crude rich companies such as YPF YPFd.SA, ARCO and British Petroleum."
"However, looking beyond the bullish weekly data," Ting noted, "global inventory by the end of June...exceeded 3.6 billion barrels...a seven year high."

The American Petroleum Institute and the Department of Energy reported Tuesday and Wednesday a drop in U.S. crude oil stocks of 9.7 million barrels per day (bpd) and 9.9 million bpd, respectively. Both also reported declines of nearly four million barrels in gasoline stocks.

Some analysts, pointing to a steady level of crude imports and a slight decline in U.S. refinery runs, said the apparent big decline in crude stocks may have been due to the short-term effect of Hurricane Danny last week or a statistical quirk.
In any case, "long term inventory trends are not so positive," Ting wrote. "The elisuve Iraqi export may start in approximately a week resulting in a significant export increase."
He also noted that distillate inventories -- primarily heating oil and diesel -- are nine percent above their level globally at this time last year.
Typically, heating oil supercedes gasoline as the main market factor after July.
